regime.summary: Easing cycle in progress: policy rate 10.5% after a 50bp cut on 2025-12-15, CPI 5.6% and flat, so real rates stay high and room to ease remains. The index is already up 58.9% in 12 months and 8.8% in one month, so the tide is favourable but the easy money is made. Funding is domestic: mutual funds buying, banks and foreigners selling. No measured timing edge either way.

6M T-bill minus policy rate -0.34pp (market near policy rate)

exposure_reason: Core default (about 75%) weighed against 70%: the index is up 58.9% in 12 months and 8.8% in one month, banks/DFIs sold $74mn and foreign corporates sold in the last 5 sessions while only mutual funds bought, so I trim about five points for a cash reserve. No situation type in the base rates gives a timing signal and the easing cycle is intact, so I do not go lower: no measured edge is not a reason to hold cash.
not_known: Reserves, current account, IMF status and next MPC date are not in the bundle. Nothing on management quality, sponsor record, balance sheets or float for the core names. The direction of the SYS insider trades and the nature of the TREET material items are not shown.
contamination_note: I have no specific recollection of events after 2026-01-09 that I used; if any influenced the choice of names it was not deliberately applied and every claim is cited to the bundle. base_rates.csv is flagged as measured partly after this date, so I used only verdict words as rough type-level odds and ignored its compounders rows.
